_doc: Phượng Minh Cung: Nguyên Anh, Kết Đan and the dead. Trúc Cơ in phuong_minh.2.cast.json, Luyện Khí in phuong_minh.3.cast.json. Seat moved to Hỏa Ti Trấn (449) in 1162; see phuong_minh.md.

people.gloss: The phoenix sings to the morning sun (Thi Kinh)
people.role: Head of Phượng Minh Cung; keeper of the Tiêu Thiều Quản
people.appearance: Small and quick, with the red-gold colouring of the vent birds and a laugh that carries across a hall; she keeps the panpipes in a plain cloth bag in her sleeve and has never been seen to open it.
people.backstory: Hoa Triêu Dương was born at dawn on the shore of Triêu Hà Hồ in 950 as the clouds turned red (A261), a lake fisher's daughter. The founder Ngô Thê Đồng (ngo_the_dong), then 620, came down from the ridge to see the child the plain was talking about and took her at nine, the last child he raised himself. A Fire like hers is rare on the lake shore, and the ridge could not feed it. In 1100 he gave her the palace (C181) and, dying, the Tiêu Thiều Quản, with the order never to play it in full (C182). She fought the Cinnabar Vein War from 1150 and won it when Doãn Ngọc Hành (doan_ngoc_hanh) brought the Pivot in on her side (C189, C190). In 1162 she moved the head's court down to the Fire Court at Hỏa Ti (N-phuong_minh-12), saying the palace had sat on Metal for seven hundred years and burned nothing but itself. When Thính Vũ's first elder Quan Vũ Thanh (quan_vu_thanh) came in secret to talk of peace in 1185 (A278), she gave her no answer in public. The private one, drafted by her chief disciple Trình Hi Quang (trinh_hi_quang) and handed over at the Wutong Court by Vu Ngô Đồng, offered peace for a fifth of Kinh Lôi Mạch's yield (N-phuong_minh-13). The Tower has never replied. She keeps Băng Tâm's Red Plum in the Hall of Spoils and tells Nhiếp Tẫn Sa (nhiep_tan_sa) it goes back when it will buy something.
people.wants: To make Phượng Minh what its name promises: the sect whose coming means the age is well governed, standing beside the Pivot as the south's judge rather than beneath it.
people.secret: In 1154, the night before Doãn Ngọc Hành decided to bring Thiên Xu into the war, she played him the first eight movements of the Shao on the Tiêu Thiều Quản in the ridge palace. She has never known whether he came for the Compact or for the music, and Thiên Xu destroyed a sect for less. He took the pipes for a ridge flute and has never asked.

people.role: Grand elder; keeper of the Nest and the Ash Seat at Chúc Dung Khẩu
people.appearance: Tall and stooped, with the white crust of old salt burns up both forearms; he wears a vent attendant's plain hemp and goes barefoot on the hot rock.
people.backstory: Nhiếp Tẫn Sa was born in 690 over a lamp-oil shop in Lai Nghi Thành and became the disciple of Lâu Liệt Hà (lau_liet_ha) at fourteen. At thirty-four he stood in the siege line at Cô Thành (A118), and when the plum-blossom riders of Lãnh Hương Các came out of the desert to break it (V071) he burned the first of them out of the saddle (N-phuong_minh-05). Two years later, when the fortress fell (C143), he walked into its hall and found a red sword laid across a heap of ash with a note in red ink: for Phó Thanh Mai's son, in the Pavilion, if he lives (N-phuong_minh-06). He knew then whose father he had killed. His master hung the sword in the Hall of Spoils and forbade its name. Nhiếp asked the founder Ngô Thê Đồng (ngo_the_dong) three times for it and was refused three times, because to return it would be to admit that the palace had destroyed a sect it held no writ against. He reached Nguyên Anh in 950, lit the ember censer at the mouth of Chúc Dung Khẩu, and has kept the Nest since, sitting beside every elder who breaks through. He asks Hoa Triêu Dương (hoa_trieu_duong) for the sword every New Year. He has heard that Phó Ám Hương (pho_am_huong) has twenty years left.
people.wants: To carry the Red Plum to Phó Ám Hương himself, tell him who burned his father, and let Phó decide what follows.
people.secret: The rider he burned out of the saddle at Cô Thành in 724 was Phó Thanh Mai. He still carries the red-ink note folded in his sleeve.

people.gloss: Wings spread wide (the phoenix's wing-mark is righteousness)
people.role: War elder; master of the Hall of Righteousness (Nghĩa Đường)
people.appearance: Broad and grey-bearded, with a lightning scar like a fern down his left side and one fan of a pair always at his belt.
people.backstory: Sử Hoành Dực was born at the Fire Court in 935, a fan-maker's son, and learned the Feather Fan from Hề Bính Hỏa (he_binh_hoa). He followed his master into the Thunder Vein War. At Thủ Lôi Bảo in 1042 (V161) Hề burned the fort and was killed by the lightning stored in it (N-phuong_minh-09); Sử, a hundred and seven, carried the body out with his own side split by the same bolt. His Dao partner Dụ Đan Huỳnh (du_dan_huynh) was his master's other disciple. They married in 1100 and had the twin fans made. In 1154, in the Cinnabar Vein War, Thính Vũ's war elder Cố Dạ Lan (co_da_lan) killed her on the vein at Đan Sơn Mạch and took her fan (N-phuong_minh-10). Sử broke through to Nguyên Anh in the field four years later, and has commanded the Hall of Righteousness since. He has told the head plainly that if she makes peace with Thính Vũ while Cố Dạ Lan lives and the right wing hangs in the Tower, he will take the Hall's disciples up to the ridge and hold the western march without her. His daughter Sử Niệm Huỳnh (su_niem_huynh) wants the peace.
people.wants: Cố Dạ Lan dead and the right wing back beside the left; failing that, war with Thính Vũ while he can still lead it.
people.secret: In council in 1090 he spoke for keeping Băng Tâm's red sword hidden. He knows the palace holds it the way the Tower holds his wife's fan, and cannot stand to hear it said.

people.gloss: The parasol tree where the phoenix perches
people.role: First elder; keeper of the Wutong Court (the old seat) and the palace's spirit birds
people.appearance: A big, loud man in a green robe streaked with bird lime, with a red-crested spirit bird on each shoulder and seeds in every pocket.
people.backstory: Vu Ngô Đồng was born in a bamboo-cutters' camp in Tử Trúc Lâm in 880, with a Fire the bamboo country seldom breeds. The founder Ngô Thê Đồng (ngo_the_dong) named him and took him at eleven, because the ridge birds came down to the boy's hand. He has kept the palace's spirit birds for three hundred years: the red-crested messengers that carry its writs, and the fighting birds that roost in the great wutong. When Hoa Triêu Dương (hoa_trieu_duong) moved the court down to the Fire Court in 1162 (N-phuong_minh-12), she left him the ridge palace as the Wutong Court, with the Hall of Rites, the western march and the Seal of the Wutong. He will not send the seal down. In 1185 he received Thính Vũ's secret envoys there and handed Quan Vũ Thanh (quan_vu_thanh) the head's terms (N-phuong_minh-13). He feeds half the ridge, lends birds to Bách Vũ Các (ta_thanh_loan) and forgets to ask for them back, and the ridge loves him for it. He has been stuck at the late stage of Kết Đan for thirty years.
people.wants: To see the head come back up the ridge, and to reach Nguyên Anh before the tree dies.
people.secret: The great wutong the old palace is built around is dying. For thirty years he has fed it his own Wood qi every night, and that is why his Kết Đan has stopped.

people.gloss: Mulberry; she who carries on the silk
people.role: Keeper of the Nest Array, the fire-silk lattice that carries the vent's fire into the seat
people.appearance: A thin woman with burn-calloused fingertips and a reel of grey thread always turning in one hand.
people.backstory: Tang Kế Ti is the ninth keeper of the Nest Array and the sixth from her family. In 590 the palace burned Hỏa Ti Trấn, the fire-silk town at the vent's foot (V165). In 592 a reeler's girl of twenty, Tang Sơ Ti (tang_so_ti), dug the last unburned hanks out of the sheds and gave them to the founder, who laid them as the array's threads from the mouth of Chúc Dung Khẩu to the Fire Court and vowed that no silk would be reeled at these vents again (N-phuong_minh-04). The silk has carried the vent's fire into the palace for six hundred years, and it is wearing out. Tang learned the array from Nhiếp Tẫn Sa (nhiep_tan_sa) and knows every strand by its heat; forty have charred through in her keeping. Since she may not reel new silk, she splices in the vent-less silk that Chức Hà Các weaves, which her son Tang Tục Lạc (tang_tuc_lac) brings home from its head Thân Vân Cẩm (than_van_cam). It holds a season, then chars.
people.wants: To mend the Nest Array before it fails, without being the keeper who broke the founder's vow; and Chức Hà's silk bound to the Nest by her son's marriage, at the palace's price, for sixty years.
people.secret: Last winter, alone at night, she reeled one hank of new fire-silk at the vent's mouth. It holds. She has told no one, and she means to reel more. When her son asked Thân Vân Cẩm to marry him, she named the dowry: all the pavilion's silk to the Nest at the palace's set price for sixty years. With every bolt of Chức Hà's in her splices, any strand that holds can be written down as theirs.

people.gloss: The Shao, and the phoenix's stately coming (Thư Kinh)
people.role: Master of the Hall of Rites (Lễ Đường) at the Wutong Court: music, funerals, the score archive
people.appearance: A long-faced woman with a musician's flat fingertips and a habit of tapping out a beat on whatever is in front of her.
people.backstory: Liên Thiều Nghi was born at the Fire Court in 1020, where her father, a Thiều Âm Thị flute-seller, sold to the inner gate. She is four generations down from Liên Khánh Dao (lien_khanh_dao), the founder's Dao partner, the Vân Môn musician who wrote down what her scattered people remembered of the Shao. Ngô Thê Đồng (ngo_the_dong) taught her himself in his last century on the ridge. She has run the Hall of Rites at the Wutong Court since 1110: the dawn flute, the funerals, the score archive and the ash rite on Quy Vũ Lĩnh. She believes the Shao was never evil, only the hands that played it, and that the palace's fear of it is the founder's fear and not a teaching. Her ancestor died in 760 trying the eighth movement (N-phuong_minh-07). Liên has rebuilt the eighth from the broken chimes of Kích Khánh Đường, which still ring when stepped on (V133), and has not dared to play it. She wants the Vân Môn Khánh, the chime lost in Vân Môn Thành (C050), to check her notes against.
people.wants: The Shao restored whole and played openly as the palace's rite music, and the Vân Môn Khánh found to prove her reading.
people.secret: She suspects the head holds the Tiêu Thiều Quản: one night in 1154 she heard pipes through the ridge palace's walls playing a movement her score does not have.

people.role: The head's chief disciple; runs the Hall of Virtue (Đức Điện) for her
people.appearance: Neat, soft-spoken and handsome, with ink on his right hand and a go stone he turns over in his left.
people.backstory: Trình Hi Quang was born at the Fire Court in 1075 to two outer-gate stewards and became Hoa Triêu Dương's (hoa_trieu_duong) disciple at twelve. He reached Kết Đan in 1165 on a foundation the Nest calls flawless, and he has been her hands in the Hall of Virtue ever since: he drafts her letters, sits at her go board and beats her one game in three. In 1185, when Quan Vũ Thanh (quan_vu_thanh) came in secret (A278), he drafted the head's private terms, peace for a fifth of Kinh Lôi Mạch's yield, and Vu Ngô Đồng (vu_ngo_dong) handed them over at the Wutong Court (N-phuong_minh-13). No reply has come in fifteen years. The head reads the silence as a refusal. Trình does not: the guest elder Chử Trì Âm (chu_tri_am) writes to Quan, and her letters never mention the terms. Sử Hoành Dực (su_hoanh_duc) does not know there were any.
people.wants: A peace with Thính Vũ signed in his hand, with the right wing fan returned in the same treaty.
people.secret: He has guessed that Quan Vũ Thanh never gave the terms to her head. He has not told his master, because she would send them by another road; he means to carry the next offer himself, with a clause he added on his own: the Tower returns the right wing fan.

people.cause: a failed breakthrough to Hóa Thần on the ridge, at 770
people.role: Founder of Phượng Minh Cung (480, at 150); died on the ridge, where the Wutong Court keeps his ashes
people.backstory: Ngô Thê Đồng was born in 330 in Ngọc Quản Trấn, the jade-pipe makers' town below Cửu Thiều Cung, and was eleven when the Pivot destroyed the palace and his family left with everyone else (V138). He wandered for a hundred and forty years as a flute-playing cultivator, and came back at 150 to found Phượng Minh Cung on the empty ridge (C009). He opened Thiều Âm Thị (A238), found the Tiêu Thiều Quản in the palace ruins in 485 and told no one (C097), and swore the North Star Compact in 510 (C107). His Dao partner was the Vân Môn musician Liên Khánh Dao (lien_khanh_dao). In 584 he asked the Pivot for the Compact's first writ against Xích Thành Môn, which had burned eleven villages (C118), and in 590 he destroyed it and Chu Liệt Nhật (chu_liet_nhat) with it (C119). In 592 he raised the Fire Court on the ashes of Hỏa Ti Trấn and sent his inner gate down to it (N-phuong_minh-03), but he never moved his own seat off the ridge. He fought the Desert Road War, joined the Pirate Purge, and in his old age lost the Thunder Vein War (C179). He died on the ridge in 1100 at 770 (C181) and gave Hoa Triêu Dương (hoa_trieu_duong) the pipes with the order never to play them in full (C182).

people.role: Master of the Hall of Benevolence (Nhân Đường): granaries, healers, the outer gate's rice
people.appearance: A short, sun-browned man who still rolls his trousers to the knee and walks the paddies before every council.
people.backstory: A paddy farmer's son from Thủy Điền Thôn, Điền Phong Niên was the founder's (ngo_the_dong) last steward and has kept the Hall of Benevolence since 1100: the granaries of Hoàng Vân Thành, the outer gate's rice and the palace's healers. In 1060, a Trúc Cơ clerk of seventy, he opened the granaries to Băng Tâm's famine on his own seal (A262). The council fined him a year's stipend, and the founder paid it. He trades rice for Lễ Tuyền's wine with Mai Lễ Tuyền (mai_le_tuyen) and has never once won the bargain.

people.appearance: A sharp-chinned woman whose lips are stained red from tasting cinnabar, with a fever flush she never loses.
people.backstory: Ash-born at the Fire Court and taught by Nhiếp Tẫn Sa (nhiep_tan_sa), Kế Chu Sa brews the palace's pills on Chu Sa Tuyền, where the jungle spring runs hot and red. Every breakthrough pill the Nest watches comes from her furnace. She has failed Vu Ngô Đồng's (vu_ngo_dong) Nguyên Anh pill twice, because its chief herb is the seed of a living wutong and the great tree on the ridge has not seeded in thirty years. She resents Đồng Hồng Lô (dong_hong_lo), who brews over a volcano for Thúy Vi and sells to Băng Tâm through Viên Chước (vien_chuoc).

people.role: Master of the Hall of Trust (Tín Đường): treasury, the Hall of Spoils, tribute and envoys
people.appearance: A handsome, heavy-lidded woman in brocade the colour of old embers, who carries the Hall of Spoils' three keys on a red cord.
people.backstory: A Lai Nghi Thành silk-broker's daughter and the head's (hoa_trieu_duong) eldest disciple, Vưu Cẩm Thư keeps the palace's money: the vassals' tribute, the port dues of Thạch Cơ Thành, and the Hall of Spoils, where a red sword hangs unnamed beside the empty hook of the Xích Hà Kỳ. The banner was lent to Hùng Phần Vũ (hung_phan_vu) in 1020 (C177) and she has asked for it back three times. She buys Chức Hà Các's fire-silk at a price that hurts it. The Nest costs more each year, so this spring she set ground rent on Phần Vũ's vents and pits in the palace's own seat province, and counted its standing dead as structures.

She has held Đan Sơn Mạch since 1158, three tiles from the Pivot's border, and her garrison watches Thính Vũ's scouts and the Pivot's surveyors alike.

When the Pivot's arrays closed, Hách Chu Lăng (hach_chu_lang) took him alive (N-phuong_minh-11), and he refused the Tower's ransom. He has been the palace's guest since 1160: he teaches the Hall of Righteousness how thunder fights, and writes to Quan Vũ Thanh for Trình Hi Quang (trinh_hi_quang).
